title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics by Grothendieck. It is a typed departmental announcement from the Université des Sciences et Techniques du Languedoc (Montpellier), Mathématiques, dated 23 September 1980. It gives the October 1980 programme of the 'Séminaire d'Analyse Convexe', with three talks by A. Fougères:
- 2 Oct. 1980, 9 h, salle 431: 'Optimisation convexe dans les Banach non-réflexifs. Méthode de relaxation-projection.'
- 9 Oct. 1980 (after G. Bouchitté): 'Inf-convolution exacte et relaxation-projection. Approximation dans le problème de minimisation.'
- 16 Oct. 1980 (after G. Bouchitté): 'Relaxation-projection et hypersurfaces minima : état du problème.'

The handwritten '159' at bottom left is an archival foliation number. The sheet sits between two pages of Teichmüller-tower computations: presentations of SL(2,Z) and GL(2,Z) by ε0, ε1, r0 and lifts to the mapping class group Γ_{1,1}. Most likely Grothendieck reused the back of a circulated departmental flyer as scrap paper, and the verso was scanned. Only the recto is shown here, and it carries no Grothendieck mathematics.

The seminar topics belong to convex analysis and the calculus of variations of the Montpellier school (Moreau, Fougères, Bouchitté). They concern relaxation of variational problems in non-reflexive spaces such as BV and L^1, inf-convolution, and minimal hypersurfaces. They are unrelated to the surrounding pages.

ideas.what: Relaxation-projection method for convex minimization in non-reflexive Banach spaces, with links to inf-convolution and minimal hypersurfaces (seminar titles only, not Grothendieck's work)
ideas.modern_name: Relaxation of convex integral functionals (lower semicontinuous envelopes, BV/L^1 settings), inf-convolution
ideas.usually_credited_to: A. Fougères, G. Bouchitté and the Montpellier convex analysis school (J.-J. Moreau), around 1980
ideas.where_published: Not Grothendieck's work; seminar announcement only

deep.surprise_reason: This is an administrative seminar announcement, probably reused as scrap paper, with no Grothendieck mathematics. Its only interest is as material evidence that the Teichmüller notes were written on recycled departmental flyers, giving a terminus post quem of late September 1980 for this sheet.
transcription_corrections: The transcription is accurate. '159' is a handwritten archival folio number at bottom left, not part of the typed text.
